market_holds: Spot $5.325 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-11 18:08 UTC), 56% below the 52-week high. No option chain, so there is no implied move. The baseline's 5.5% 'usual move' comes from 6-K text matches, and its cadence check marks those as mostly not earnings. The three real prints since the February IPO opened at -7.4% (Q4, 2026-03-24), -2.0% (Q1, 2026-05-06) and -9.7% (Q2, 2026-08-06) against the prior close; I computed these from Yahoo daily bars. The 20-day run-up of -26% is mostly macro. The ADR fell 37.6% on 2026-10-26 (7.58 to 4.73, 3.4m shares traded), the Monday after Lula's runoff win. The same day EWZ fell 19.8%, INTR 35%, STNE 27% and PAGS 25%. Since then AGBK is up 13% (to 5.34) while EWZ is down 5%, INTR down 16% and BRL 11% weaker. It rose 4.7% today and 7.8% over five days into the print. Support comes from a 3-million-share buyback announced 2026-10-27, about 2% of shares or roughly five days of volume. Consensus: Itau BBA expects Q3 net income of about R$200m and ROE of 17%. That is flat against Q2's R$200.3m, which a tax line flattered (pre-tax R$115m). Itau BBA has cut its 2026 and 2027 estimates by 5% and 9%. XP (2026-10-28) cut 2027 by 3% and expects INSS origination to normalise only from Q4 26. Aggregator EPS figures range from $0.28 (TipRanks, 2 analysts) to $0.33 (EarningsWhispers). The company gives no formal guide. Its Q2 letter said it expected 'sequentially stronger earnings beginning in the third quarter, with a more pronounced financial contribution in the fourth quarter'. Short interest was 3.3% of float (Stocktitan, undated).
view: This is a Brazilian INSS payroll lender trading near 1x book. The macro shock has reset its price: the election runoff that took a third off the ADR in one session, a weaker real, and Selic cuts the market now sees pausing. The Q3 release covers July to September, which is before that shock. The reaction will turn on three things. First, pre-tax profit and cost of risk, since Q2 pre-tax fell 47% QoQ on front-loaded provisions and costs. Second, whether net income clears the roughly R$200m bar that the sell side has already cut. Third, the call: post-election regulation of INSS lending, funding costs, and buyback execution. Two things favour a pop. The bar was lowered after management promised sequential improvement, and the stock sits at a depressed multiple after an election overshoot. Two things lean the other way. Every print since the IPO has opened lower, each time because pre-tax quality fell short of management's tone. And XP's note says lending was weak for two quarters because of biometric rules and thinner payroll margins. I found no fresh, independent datapoint for the quarter itself (origination, market share or NPL after June) that the price might be missing. The decisive line is therefore unobservable before the release, and the pattern of past reactions is too short (three prints) to bet on. No edge I can show.

recommendation.reason: The bar (Itau BBA about R$200m) has been cut, while management guided to sequential improvement, and that argues for a beat. Every post-IPO print has opened lower on pre-tax quality, and that argues against. I found no dated datapoint since the Q2 call that the price does not already hold, and Brazil macro and election risk dominate the tape. Neither direction reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Pre-tax profit clearly above Q2's R$115m with cost of risk falling and net income well above R$200m, plus a call that plays down post-election regulatory risk, would make me lean long. A pre-tax miss or cost of risk above 6% would confirm the short-leaning pattern.

self_critique: The case for long: the ADR fell nearly twice as much as EWZ on the election and trades at about 1x book and under 4x XP's 2027 earnings. Estimates have just been cut while management promised sequential improvement, and buyback support is active. The first post-election print could reprice it 10%+ if tone is confident. The case for short: three of three negative opens, cost of risk still high, and a Lula government that has already suspended this lender once. Either could be right. Neither has evidence I can date that the price lacks.
